title: Scalable AI Foundations for Automated Synapse Detection and Cross-Species Comparative Connectomics in Petascale EM Volumes
background:
Volumetric electron microscopy (vEM) has reached a regime where whole-brain or large-region reconstructions of Drosophila, larval zebrafish, and cubic-millimeter mammalian cortex are routinely acquired at 4-8 nm resolution, producing petabyte-scale datasets that vastly outpace manual proofreading capacity. Recent flagship efforts, including the FlyWire whole-brain reconstruction [1] and the H01 human temporal lobe volume [2], have established that flood-filling networks and affinity-based agglomeration can achieve near-human accuracy on neurite segmentation, while transformer-based synapse detectors [3] now reach >95% F1 on intra-dataset benchmarks. Comparative analyses across species have begun to reveal conserved motifs in sensory microcircuits [4], suggesting that connectomics can move from descriptive cataloguing toward quantitative cross-species circuit science.

Despite this progress, three coupled bottlenecks prevent connectomics from scaling to population-level and cross-species studies. First, synapse detectors trained on one staining protocol or species generalize poorly to others, with reported F1 drops of 20-40 points under domain shift [3][5], forcing costly per-dataset re-annotation. Second, post-segmentation proofreading still consumes the majority of human effort; current active-learning approaches reduce edits by ~30% but lack principled uncertainty quantification at the circuit-motif level [5]. Third, comparative connectomics lacks rigorous statistical and representational frameworks: existing graph-matching pipelines [6] operate on pairwise neuron correspondences and do not scale to whole-brain comparisons across non-isomorphic nervous systems, nor do they couple structural motifs to functional or transcriptomic priors. Closing these gaps requires AI methods that are simultaneously sample-efficient, uncertainty-aware, biologically grounded, and tractable at petascale.
challenges: Designing self-supervised and domain-adaptive representations for vEM that transfer synapse and organelle detection across staining protocols, microscopes (ssTEM, FIB-SEM, MultiSEM), and species without per-dataset retraining of millions of labels.

Developing calibrated, circuit-aware uncertainty estimation for neurite segmentation and synapse assignment, so that proofreading effort can be routed to edits that materially change downstream connectivity statistics rather than to cosmetic boundary errors.

Building scalable graph-learning frameworks for comparative connectomics that align non-isomorphic connectomes via motif- and cell-type-conditioned embeddings, integrate transcriptomic and functional priors, and provide statistical tests for conserved versus divergent circuit structure across species.

Engineering petascale training and inference infrastructure that supports billion-node, trillion-edge connectome graphs with reproducible benchmarks, FAIR data standards, and tooling usable by neuroscience labs without dedicated ML engineering staff.
